mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the prior month's level coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its prior month's value by at least 0.25 percentage points
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a zero return baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggests softening labor market pressure and disinflation, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous month AND CPIAUCSL < previous month
failure_condition: In 60-day windows where the trigger occurs, 20-day forward returns are negative on average, or the interaction rank IC exceeds 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive month of rising home building permits (INDPRO) and a sustained decline in retail sales (HOUST) indicate strengthening construction demand while weakening consumer demand, producing a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate sector rotation.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases for 2 consecutive months AND HOUST decreases for 3 consecutive months
regime_hint: Construction cycle acceleration with consumer weakness
failure_condition: Across 20-day windows during the trigger, 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below trend coincides with a decline in consumer confidence (unavailable proxy at decision time), but the combination of falling output and rising unemployment (UNRATE) signals supply-side softness that pushes 5-day S&P 500 forward returns negative.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by at least 0.2 percentage points AND INDPRO is two standard deviations below its 12-month moving average
failure_condition: Over 20-day windows where the trigger is met, 5-day forward returns are not consistently negative (average positive or flat).

mechanism_narrative: During a period of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS below 2% and UNRATE below 6.5%), the 60-day S&P 500 forward return tends to be positive as lower policy rates lower discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: In 60-day windows under the regime, 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a zero-return baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in job openings (not directly observable at decision time) is proxied by a sharp drop in unemployment (UNRATE) followed by a rebound in payrolls (PAYEMS), creating a bullish reversal signal for the S&P 500 over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by at least 0.3 percentage points and PAYEMS increases by at least 5,000 in the following month
regime_hint: Labor market transition from contraction to expansion
failure_condition: In 60-day windows with the trigger, 20-day forward returns are negative on average or the interaction rank IC exceeds 0.1.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-time decline in retail sales (HOUST) followed by a sustained rise in consumer spending (not directly observable) is anticipated to trigger a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market participants expect demand to recover.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by at least 10% from the prior month in a single month
failure_condition: Over 20-day windows after the trigger, 5-day forward returns remain negative or flat across 70% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip in industrial production (INDPRO) declines—first a sharp drop, then a partial rebound—while inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains stable, creates uncertainty about supply chain normalization and tends to produce negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two consecutive months, then rises but remains below its prior month's level, AND CPIAUCSL is within 1% of its prior month's value
failure_condition: In 60-day windows with the trigger, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).
